S056-01.notes: 'Haphazard' matches the early critics' reading that the composer 'could no longer hold a piece together.' A (derivative) is about originality, not coherence. B (austere) and D (melancholy) could describe the music's tone but don't match the claim of declining structural control.

S056-02.notes: A shows both parts of the conclusion: species A rises 12->25->41%, and species B stays flat at 29-31%. B, C and D are all true of the table, but none shows the distance pattern for A together with its absence for B. D wrongly lumps the species together. The Janzen-Connell summary (specialist enemies gather near the parent and lower survival close by) is accurate.

S056-03.notes: A single clay source points to making the pots in one place and then distributing them, which is an alternative to a shared culture. A contradicts the single-source finding. C overreaches to 'many regions.' B has nothing to do with the argument.

S056-04.notes: The list items contain internal commas, so they must be separated by semicolons, matching 'Lionel Park, a geologist;'. A gives a comma splice inside the list and makes it ambiguous. C puts a colon in the middle of the list. D runs 'a botanist Lionel Park' together.

S056-05.notes: 'Two' requires the plural, and 'findings' requires the possessive, so the answer is researchers'. B is singular. C has no possessive. D is malformed.

S056-06.notes: Baudelaire's remark supports and illustrates the critics' dismissal, so 'Indeed' fits. A, B and D wrongly signal contrast; the mention of 'arts' may tempt test takers toward a contrast. The 1859 Salon 'very humble servant' of the sciences and arts quote is accurately represented.

S056-07.notes: Only B states both findings and contrasts them. C gives only the 2018 finding. D notes the shared topic without giving a contrast. A describes the setup only. The facts match the record: Mischel's Stanford Bing nursery school studies, and Watts, Duncan & Quan 2018.

S056-08.notes: Silence from a man who is always certain is ominous, and it unsettles the villagers more than an explicit warning would have. A ('proves') overstates; the text doesn't establish the ice condition. B has no support. C is the opposite of the intended effect.

S056-09.notes: The surprising finding is that colonies unable to read the dance sometimes did as well as normal colonies, and B sets this against the dance's expected purpose. C is the expected result. A and D give background only. The facts are consistent with the record: von Frisch's decoding, and the disoriented-dance experiments (e.g., Sherman & Visscher 2002) in which the benefit varied by season.
